AN INTERESTING COLLECTION OF VIOLIN AND VIOLONCELLO TEMPLATES, by J. M. Somny, London including bow templates, the violin and violoncello soundholes and heads and details of corners and archings, a large collection (about 80)  Joseph Maurice Somny was born at Mirecourt (Vosges) in France and worked for W. E. Hill & Sons, Hanwell from 1888-1910 and later at 90 George Street, Baker Street, London, died 1931. He was rated as the finest restorer of his time; when a famous violin passed through his hands he would make woodcut patterns of its details as a reminder of that instrument, these are now collector's items and are evidence of Somny’s remarkable skill. See R. L. Lewin, ‘Diary of a restorer’, The Strad, September 1969, a copy of which is included with these templates
